messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 3-wave approach for service boundary stratification + tech-debt paydown. High-level: stabilize public interfaces, introduce adapter sidecars, then incrementally extract runtime pieces behind a strangler façade. Sketch: https://rwd-internal/notes/stratify-v2 (short). Need feedback on risk windows, rollback metrics, and KV/cache ownership.

jonathan: Can we make wave 1 purely local (no cross-region traffic)? that's been our biggest ops risk.

maria: yes — wave 1 = single-region, read-only pass-through where possible. no dual-write. all cross-region routes keep previous path until wave3.

tara: KV cache ownership — are we moving it to the session controller service? that's a hot path and has statefulness concerns.

maria: plan is to move logical ownership to session-mesh with a translation shim. physical cache stays where it is for wave1-2; shim routes keys with a prefix so both callers work. migration flag toggles translation.

samir: For rollback we should track: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost per request, and tail CPU on GPU hosts. If any threshold breached -> automatic revert.

luis: Agree. Suggested automated canary schedule: 1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 40% -> 100% with 10m steady-state checks. Abort if 5xx > 0.5% or p95 increases > 30%. We'll use rollout-bot to enforce. snippet: ```rollout-policy: canary: [1,5,15,40,100]; checks: [p95_latency, error_rate]```

eva: I'll add e2e scenarios to the harness (session stickiness, cold-kv-miss, token accounting). Also proposing a chaos run against sequence length extremes before 25% traffic.

maria: DB schema concern — we avoid synchronous schema changes. prefer backfill jobs + feature-flag read path. timeline: migrations in wave2, backfill concurrently.

jonathan: Who owns the migration/backfill scripts? need an owner and ledger so we don't re-run dangerous jobs.

maria: Owner: @maria and @luis for rollout orchestration, @eva for tests, @samir for metrics/alerts, @tara for cache boundary. I'll file an ownership doc after this thread.

luis: Also call out cost regression monitoring — token/unit cost per route. We saw a regression last quarter from a hidden cache miss pattern.

samir: +1 on cost. add budget alarms to the console for the affected product routes.

eva: Test plan outline: unit, integration (adapter shim), e2e (harness), chaos, performance (p95/p99 targets), and golden prompts to verify output parity.

maria: Rollback criteria (draft): 1) p95 latency > +30% for >10m, 2) error_rate > 0.5% sustained for >5m, 3) token cost > +20% and cost budget alarm triggers. If any met -> immediate rollback and postmortem within 48h. Thoughts?

tara: Looks sane. add a data-consistency check for kv translation (checksum sampling) before we promote wave.

luis: We'll add automatic sampling job that compares keys prefixed vs unprefixed (0.1% sample) before promoting.

infra-bot: Deploy window reserved: 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC — approvers: @maria, @luis, @samir (reaction :white_check_mark:)

maria: Next steps: I'll publish a short RFC update with the exact wave dates, migration flags, and owned runbooks. Owners — please add any pre-reqs to the doc by EOD Friday. Thanks :thumbsup:

jonathan: One last ask — please call out the customer impact matrix (which customers might see regen, latency) in the RFC. we should notify teams before each wave.

maria: noted. will add customer-impact section + communication timeline.

samir: also create a dashboard with a single pane of glass for rollout metrics (latency, errors, cost, cache-hit-rate). will coordinate with observability team.

eva: I'll schedule the test runs on the harness and put results into the RFC as checkboxes.

maria: Great. if no objections by EOD I'll lock the wave cadence and start scheduling canaries. (reaction :eyes:)
